---
title: "The exchange contract"
---


zotQDA, qdaZ, qdaR and qdaPy are four code bases that have to agree on the
same files. The agreement is written down in a form a machine can check:
`contract/exchange-v1.json`, generated from a single declaration in the
plugin and shipped by every consumer.

This package installs its copy as `inst/extdata/exchange-v1.json`:

```r
ct <- qda_contract()
ct$version
names(ct$formats)
qda_formats()
```

## The nine formats

| Format | File | One row per |
|---|---|---|
| `fragments/1` | `zotqda-fragments.csv` | annotation x code |
| `uncoded/1` | `zotqda-uncoded.csv` | annotation with no code |
| `codebook/1` | `zotqda-codebook.csv` | code |
| `history/1` | `zotqda-history.csv` | log event (add and remove) |
| `abbrevs/1` | `zotqda-abbrevs.csv` | code abbreviation |
| `consensus-mapping/1` | `zotqda-konsens-abbildung.csv` | coder code to consensus code |
| `consensus-protocol/1` | `zotqda-konsens-codesystem.csv` | consensus decision |
| `consensus-metrics/1` | `zotqda-konsens-kennzahlen.csv` | coder pair, mean, round |
| `multi-coded/1` | `zotqda-mehrfachkodierungen.csv` | multiply coded segment |

Column lists live in the contract file itself, so this page cannot drift out of
date about them — `qda_formats()` reads them from the shipped copy.

## Reference files and their expected parse

`inst/extdata/` holds one sample per format plus `expected.json`, which states
what a correct reader must produce. The samples deliberately contain what a
naive `strsplit(x, ",")` gets wrong: embedded quotes, the delimiter inside a
field, and a line break inside a field.

`tests/testthat/test-contract.R` walks all nine and compares field by field.
Passing that means this reader agrees with the plugin on encoding, quoting,
line breaks and the byte-order mark, the four things two CSV implementations
usually differ about.

## Changing the contract

The declaration lives in the plugin, not here. A new version means:

1. change `src/exchange.js` in zotQDA, the single declaration;
2. regenerate the contract, samples and expectations there;
3. copy the new contract and samples into `inst/extdata/`;
4. raise the version this package accepts, and handle the change.

Adding a column is a minor change: readers address columns by name and ignore
what they do not know, so `strict = TRUE` still passes. Removing or renaming a
column, or changing what one means, requires a new version number, at which
point this package should refuse the file until it has been taught the
difference.
